newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mostly lower, near lows.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mostly lower, near lows.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended lower and hugging day's lows after a bevy of officials' remarks and U.S. economic data kept players edgy.
Languid afternoon trade picked up at the close as offers kept most nearby units stuck near session lows, which also constituted a new contract low at $0.5834 in March marks.
That level corresponded roughly to 1.7150, a level some traders said the dollar likely would have trouble scaling.
March Swiss francs slunk lower but respected its contract low at $0.6722, although a broker expected dollar/Swiss to struggle to clear 1.4900 or about $0.6720 in March futures.
Sentiment appeared skewed to the downside for currencies, given ideas that economic fundamentals favor the dollar. But opinion was divided over how smooth that path would prove.
"Technically, we should be a lot lower," said one currency floor broker. "I'm sure it's going to be a really bumpy road (for the dollar) all the way up."

"The feeling seems to be confusion," added another broker, noting the large variety of statements Monday and Tuesday from government officials. "I think it's (market) going to be wishy-washy until payrolls on Friday."
"They're not going anywhere until Friday," added a third.

Traders also wait for German unemployment figures due Thursday that are expected to show an increase in joblessness, although different press reports have predicted increasingly smaller gains in the number of unemployed.

Late Tuesday, German television said German unemployment stood at 4.671 million, smaller than the 4.7 million reported by a German newspaper Tuesday morning. Another German paper reported Sunday that unemployment would hit 4.8 million.
Various comments Tuesday by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to the House Budget Committee about consumer price index and US budget added to the uncertainty, brokers said.

Greenspan said it's crucial to keep inflation down in short run to help keep the economy running toward price stability. He also said the most likely prospect was for continued sustainable economic growth with low and stable inflation.
Traders wait for Greenspan to give the second half of the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to a House committee Wednesday.
Technically, the break below the $0.5900 area in March marks could keep prices pressured nearterm, brokers said.
"Below $0.5895 was a really big level on the futures chart," added the first floor broker, who said many customers who had been flat began selling again on the decline.

March yen settled down $0.000062 at $0.008200, marks lost $0.0057 to $0.5837, Swiss francs dropped $0.0043 to $0.6733, sterling lost $0.0048 to $1.6128, Canadian dollar fell $0.0014 to $0.7305, Aussie dollar rose $0.0021 to $0.7893, Mexican peso rose $0.000200 to $0.124300.
